sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: With reference to biological interactions between two species, identify the two wrong statements: (a) One organism benefits while the other is harmed: parasitism. (b) Both species cannot survive without the other: mutualism. (c) Penicillium secretes antibiotics which inhibit bacteria: predation. (d) One species benefits and the other is unharmed: commensalism.
questions.answer: (b) and (c) are wrong: (b) interdependence with neither able to survive is symbiosis (obligate mutualism); (c) Penicillium inhibiting bacteria is amensalism, not predation.

questions.q: Name two human activities which continuously increase the atmospheric carbon dioxide.
questions.answer: Burning of fossil fuels and deforestation.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The relationship in which one species benefits at the cost of another is ______. (b) A group of species living together in a natural area is a ______.
questions.answer: (a) parasitism. (b) community.

questions.q: Match: (a) Amensalism (b) Mutualism (c) Competition with (i) both benefit (ii) both harmed (iii) one inhibited, the other unaffected.
State true or false: (a) A snake can be a secondary as well as a tertiary consumer. (b) Energy flow in an ecosystem is cyclic.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – it is unidirectional.

questions.q: Name the two basic forms of population growth curves.
questions.answer: J-shaped (exponential) and S-shaped (sigmoid).

questions.q: Name the biotic components of a pond ecosystem.
questions.answer: Producers (phytoplankton and rooted plants), consumers (zooplankton, insect larvae, fish) and decomposers (bacteria and fungi).

questions.q: Give the levels of organisation in life from gene to biosphere.
questions.answer: Gene, cell, organ, organism, species, population, community, ecosystem, biome and biosphere.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Construct a pyramid of number in a grassland with four trophic levels.
questions.answer: From base to top: grass (producers, very many) → grasshoppers (primary consumers, many) → frogs (secondary consumers, fewer) → snakes (tertiary consumers, fewest); the pyramid is upright with a broad base.

questions.q: Write any two biotic and two abiotic components of a pond ecosystem.
questions.answer: Biotic: phytoplankton and fish. Abiotic: sunlight and water (temperature, dissolved O2).

questions.q: Explain the term commensalism with an example.
questions.answer: An association in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited; e.g. the remora fish attached to a shark, or epiphytes on trees.

questions.q: Construct a food chain showing one producer and three consumers of different trophic levels. What is the trophic level of the final consumer?
questions.answer: Grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. The snake, the final consumer, is at the fourth trophic level (tertiary consumer).

questions.q: Under what conditions do the population growth curves become J-shaped and S-shaped?
questions.answer: J-shaped when resources are unlimited (exponential growth followed by a crash); S-shaped when resources become limiting and the population stabilises at the carrying capacity.

questions.q: Distinguish between habitat and niche.
questions.answer: Habitat is the place where an organism lives (its address); niche is its functional role and use of resources (its profession).

questions.q: What is the 10 per cent law?
questions.answer: Only about 10 per cent of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next; the rest is lost as heat in respiration.

questions.q: What are decomposers? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Organisms that feed on dead organic matter and recycle nutrients; bacteria and fungi.

questions.q: State two differences between a food chain and a food web.
questions.answer: A food chain is a single linear sequence of feeding; a food web is a network of interconnected food chains and gives stability.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the characteristics of a population.
questions.answer: Density, natality, mortality, dispersal (emigration and immigration), age distribution, sex ratio and growth form; density depends on natality, mortality, immigration and emigration.

questions.q: Explain the S-shaped population growth curve.
questions.answer: A lag phase with few births; a growth phase with rapid increase when food is plentiful; a stable (plateau) phase when resources become limiting and natality equals mortality.

questions.q: Explain the energy flow in an ecosystem.
questions.answer: Solar energy is trapped by producers, passed to herbivores and carnivores; at each level energy is lost as heat in respiration; only 10 per cent passes on, so flow is unidirectional and the chain has 4-5 steps.

questions.q: Explain the types of interspecific interactions with one example each.
questions.answer: Amensalism (Penicillium and bacteria), predation (lion and deer), parasitism (Cuscuta), competition, commensalism (remora and shark) and mutualism (sea anemone and hermit crab).

questions.q: Explain the structure of a pond ecosystem.
questions.answer: Abiotic: light, temperature, water, gases, nutrients; biotic: producers (phytoplankton, rooted plants), consumers (zooplankton, fish) and decomposers (bacteria and fungi).

questions.q: Write short notes on the tropical rain forest biome.
questions.answer: Rainfall above 200 cm, high temperature and light, humus-rich soil, high turnover of nutrients, highest productivity and biomass, with epiphytes and lianas and rich fauna.

questions.q: Write any three adaptations of desert plants and animals.
questions.answer: Reduced leaves or spines, deep roots, water storage (Opuntia); camel stores fat and survives without water; burrowing rodents.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the levels of biological organisation and the concepts of habitat, niche and adaptation.
questions.answer: Gene to biosphere; habitat as address; niche as profession with examples; adaptation as a structure or behaviour helping survival, e.g. bird beaks, gills, thorns.

questions.q: Describe the food chain, trophic levels and food web.
questions.answer: Producers, primary, secondary and tertiary consumers and decomposers with examples; special feeding groups; the position of humans; the food web.

questions.q: Describe ecological pyramids and the energy flow in an ecosystem.
questions.answer: Pyramids of number, biomass and energy; 10 per cent law; energy is lost as heat; flow is one way.

questions.q: Describe the major terrestrial biomes.
questions.answer: Tropical rain forest, temperate deciduous forest, coniferous forest, grassland, desert and tundra with climate, flora and fauna.
